about: How real published Nature figures arrange their panels, measured from the owner's own PDF library. Consumed by figpipe.composite as its geometry priors: the gutter, the panel aspect and the panel-letter offset are read from here rather than invented.
method: Each figure's caption-anchored bbox is rendered at 300 dpi and binarised (ink = grey < 200). Panel letters are read from the PDF's own text spans (single characters a-h, 7-9.5 pt). Full captions come from corpus/caption_features.jsonl joined through the extraction manifests; the caption letter counter accepts only forms Nature writes: '(a)', 'a,', 'a;', 'a-c' ranges, 'Figure 1a'. The panel count is the detected letter count, falling back to the caption count, falling back to 1. For a count of n the factor pairs (rows, cols) are enumerated; a boundary starts at the next letter's position (letters sit at the panel's top-left, so the split is just left of the following letter) or at equal division, and is refined to the emptiest 0.8 mm band within +-15 mm on the ink projection. A grid is accepted when every cell holds ink and has aspect in 0.15-8. Gutters are the ink-free run around the accepted boundary, in mm.
caveats: Panel count comes from the panel letters; a figure whose letters are drawn as outlines rather than text is counted from its caption, and one with neither is recorded as a single panel. That under-counts composites rather than inventing them.

A gutter measured here is white space between INK, which includes the panels' own tick labels. The composer adds its label furniture on top of this number when axes are not shared -- see figpipe/composite.py.
The corpus of measured figures is the caption-anchored set (73 figures from 11 papers). It is the owner's library, not a random sample of Nature.
